title: Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
notes: Since we want unique ID of each user and if a user does not have a unique ID then just show null, and all the users are there in "Employees" table so we perform a simple LEFT JOIN
code:
SELECT 
    unique_id, name
FROM 
    Employees LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI
    ON Employees.id = EmployeeUNI.id;

title: Product Sales Analysis I
notes:
we were asked to report the product_name, year, and price for each sale_id in the Sales table.
so just LEFT JOIN sales table with Product table

we can also use normal JOIN ig since all the product_id of Sales table are there in Product table
code:
SELECT
    product_name, year, price
FROM
    Sales LEFT JOIN Product
    ON Sales.product_id = Product.product_id;

title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
notes:
I was asked to return the customer_id that visited and walked away without any transactions - and how many times they did this
So we LEFT JOIN the Visits and Transactions table and see where the amount is NULL and simply group by customer_id and count such customer_ids
code:
SELECT
    customer_id, COUNT(customer_id) AS count_no_trans
FROM
    Visits LEFT JOIN Transactions
    ON Visits.visit_id = Transactions.visit_id
    WHERE amount IS NULL
GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Rising Temperature
notes:
there can be multiple ways to approach this
on way is to cross join the weather table and then filtering out the rows where the date diff = 1 and temp is more

another way is to inner join the weather table on the condition that the date diff is 1 and then filter out the rows with higher tempratures
code:
-- Using Cross Join
SELECT
    w1.id
FROM
    Weather AS w1 CROSS JOIN Weather AS w2
    WHERE 
        DATEDIFF(w1.recordDate, w2.recordDate) = 1
        AND w1.temperature > w2.temperature;

-- Using Inner Join 
SELECT
    w1.id
FROM
    Weather AS w1 INNER JOIN Weather AS w2
    ON DATEDIFF(w1.recordDate, w2.recordDate) = 1
    WHERE w1.temperature > w2.temperature

title: Average Time of Process per Machine
notes: performed a INNER JOIN so that left table just consists the start time and right one the end time, then average of their difference and rounded it to 3 decimal places
code:
SELECT
    a1.machine_id, ROUND(AVG(a2.timestamp - a1.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time
FROM
    Activity a1 INNER JOIN Activity a2
    ON 
        a1.machine_id = a2.machine_id AND
        a1.process_id = a2.process_id AND
        a1.activity_type = 'start' AND
        a2.activity_type = 'end'
GROUP BY machine_id;

title: Students and Examinations
notes:
we first CROSS JOIN Students and Subjects table so that we get a table where every student is associated with every subject
then we LEFT JOIN it with examination on the condition that the student id and subject name should match - this creates duplicate rows if a student have given same exam multiple times and a null value in Examinations.subject_name if that student+subject combination does not exist in Examination table - hence we can simply GROUP BY this student id and subject name and count this Examinations.subject_name column
code:
SELECT 
    Students.student_id, Students.student_name, Subjects.subject_name, COUNT(Examinations.subject_name) AS attended_exams
FROM
    Students CROSS JOIN Subjects
    LEFT JOIN Examinations
    ON
        Students.student_id = Examinations.student_id AND
        Subjects.subject_name = Examinations.subject_name
GROUP BY Students.student_id, Subjects.subject_name
ORDER BY Students.student_id, Subjects.subject_name;
